analysis.title: From AI build-out to AI diffusion
key_insights: Tech stocks fell in the month despite substantial earnings beats and guidance raises from Arista, Coherent, Lumentum and Aehr Test Systems. The manager says the sector fell out of fashion rather than fundamentals deteriorating.
Aehr Test Systems beat on sales and margins and upgraded its 2027 revenue guide to 200%, described as the pick of the bunch among Fund tech holdings.

The Fund held a sizeable overweight to Semis and Tech Hardware through the summer. The assumption that AI keeps diffusing is intact, but the assumption that frontier model performance justifies near-term spending is under greater scrutiny.

Data centre build-out snags include under-supply of chips, power and possibly permits. Democratic governors replacing Republicans in Texas, Ohio and Georgia raised fears of moratoria across states representing about 40% of planned build-out.

The principal concern is slower revenue growth at frontier labs, the best gauge of AI diffusion. Anthropic's growth reportedly slowed in September and may not have sped up in October, so free cash flow to fund data centres is less than markets assumed in summer.
Anthropic ARR rose from $1bn in December 2024 to more than $80bn reported in October. Its own year-end 2026 estimate at the start of the year was $25bn.

Other results were strong: AMD data-centre revenue almost doubled, Palantir delivered triple digit growth again, and some infrastructure capacity is booked out to 2029. Shares fell anyway, signalling a shift from rewarding growth promise to scrutinising economics.

The manager models data centre GW against user revenues and profits to derive the return trajectory the frontier labs need. The next Anthropic and OpenAI reported figures are critical for the build-out outlook.
Valuations now price in a material slowdown in investment, which conflicts with hyperscalers guiding to higher-than-expected 2027 CapEx.
Microsoft's forward P/E has ranged 20x to 35x since 2023 with quarterly sales growth of 12% to 19%. It is now 25x forward with growth at the top of that range.
The Fund has cut exposure to AI compute builders and vendors and is broadening to AI users such as Tempus AI and Palantir, aiming to be less reliant on the lab revenue trajectory.

Palantir is highlighted via Airbus Skywise (over 100 airlines, revenue opportunity above $850m a year per independent analysis), EasyJet avoiding nearly 80 cancellations, and a FedEx Freight tech rewrite.
